info.name: my-microservices
info.description:
End-to-end collection for the Tier 1-4 microservices stack. Pair with microservices.postman_environment.json. See docs/microservices/useful-commands.md for context.

Conventions:
- Collection-level HTTP Basic auth (admin:admin123). Individual requests can override.
- Pre-request script generates `idempotencyKey` + `correlationId` per call and injects as headers (no manual UUID copy-paste).
- Tests on write endpoints capture resource ids into env vars (lastOrderId, lastSagaId, lastDlqId).

exec: // Per-request UUIDs — avoids manual regeneration between runs.

item.name: F1. Flow — Happy order (gateway → saga → Kafka)
item.description:
Walks a single order from HTTP request through the saga to a NOTIFIED terminal state.

Run top-to-bottom. Each step chains vars from the previous step via test scripts.

What each step proves:
  1. OAuth2 token exchange           → auth-server is up, demo-client credentials valid
  2. POST /orders                    → gateway routes to order-service, saga.start() fires
  3. Peek payment.commands topic     → orchestrator published PaymentCommand on Kafka
  4. Poll saga state after ~5s       → payment-service replied OK, saga = PAID or NOTIFIED
  5. Peek notification.commands      → orchestrator published NotifyUserCommand
  6. Final saga state                → NOTIFIED (success terminal)
  7. Final order status              → PAID
  8. Grafana order-saga dashboard    → eye-check the orders_saga_terminal_total counter

If step N fails, you know exactly which hop broke.

item.name: 1. OAuth2 token → accessToken
item.description: Fetches a Bearer token used by all subsequent steps. Fails here → auth-server not up or client credentials wrong.

item.name: 2. POST /api/v1/orders — fires saga
item.description:
Hits the gateway, which routes to order-service. order-service:
  - persists an Order row (status=CREATED)
  - writes an outbox row (OrderCreatedEvent)
  - calls OrderSagaOrchestrator.start() → PaymentCommand on payment.commands
Response body carries the new orderId; we store it + capture the trace header.
Response status is 201. Fail here → gateway down, Feign to product failed, DB error.

item.name: 3. kafka-ui — peek payment.commands
item.description:
Looks at the last 10 messages on payment.commands. You should see one with sagaId matching this order's saga. kafka-ui is read-only; just a peek.
Empty? → orchestrator never fired. Check order-service logs for StreamBridge errors.

exec: // Extract sagaId from the newest message if possible, store for later steps

item.name: 4. Wait ~5s, poll saga state
item.description:
The orchestrator processes PaymentReply then publishes NotifyUserCommand. Give it ~5s.
Expected state: PAID (after payment reply) or NOTIFIED (after notify reply).
Pre-request sleeps 5s so you don't need to click twice.

exec: // Sleep ~5s to let the saga advance

item.name: 5. kafka-ui — peek notification.commands
item.description:
Look for a NotifyUserCommand with matching sagaId. Empty here → payment reply never
landed (payment-service down) or orchestrator crashed between PaymentReply and
StreamBridge.send(NOTIFY_COMMANDS, ...).

exec: console.log('messages for this sagaId on notification.commands:', mine.length);

item.name: 6. Final saga state (should be NOTIFIED)
item.description: Confirms the saga reached terminal success state.

exec: // Second small sleep in case notify reply is still in flight

item.name: 7. Order status (should be PAID)
item.description: Order should be PAID when saga reached NOTIFIED.

item.name: 8. Open Grafana order-saga dashboard (eye-check)
item.description:
Just a GET on the dashboard URL to confirm Grafana is up and the dashboard exists.
Open the response's Location header or the URL in a browser — look for the
orders_saga_terminal_total{outcome="completed"} counter incrementing.

item.name: F2. Flow — Payment fails (saga FAILED)
item.description:
How to debug the payment-fail path. Two ways to trigger it:

  Option A — Simulate: stop payment-service via `docker compose stop paymentservice`,
             then run step 2 below. The in-process retry will exhaust and messages
             will head to payment.commands.DLT.
  Option B — Manually produce a PaymentReply(success=false) via kafka-ui UI
             (http://localhost:8090 → topic payment.replies → Produce Message).
             Payload: {"sagaId":"<id>","orderId":"<id>","success":false,
                       "failureReason":"insufficient_funds","paymentId":null}

What each step proves:
  1. (Same auth as F1)
  2. POST order to kick off the saga
  3. Peek payment.commands.DLT to confirm messages are being poisoned (Option A)
  4. Poll saga until state = FAILED
  5. Order status is CANCELLED
  6. orders_saga_terminal_total{outcome="failed"} metric incremented (Prometheus query)

item.name: 2. POST /orders — expect eventual FAILED
item.description: Order is created, saga starts, payment never succeeds.

item.name: 3. kafka-ui — peek payment.commands.DLT (Option A only)
item.description:
If payment-service is DOWN, in-process retry exhausts and the message heads here.
If payment-service is UP but replying success=false, no DLT activity — the reply is a normal domain outcome, not a poisoned message. In that case this step
returns an empty list (which may be the correct answer).

exec: // Capture sagaId from the latest DLT message if present

item.name: 4. Poll saga state until FAILED (give it ~15s)

exec: // Longer wait — Option A exhausts retries over ~10s

item.name: 6. Prometheus — assert failed-counter incremented
item.description: Point of this step: the DASHBOARD you built earlier is also queryable from here.

exec: const val = r.data && r.data.result && r.data.result[0] && r.data.result[0].value && r.data.result[0].value[1];

item.name: F3. Flow — Notification fails → compensation (RefundCommand)
item.description:
Payment succeeds, notification fails, orchestrator sends a RefundCommand on
payment.commands.refund. Saga transitions through COMPENSATING → FAILED.

Trigger options:
  Option A — Stop notification service: docker compose stop notification
             Then run step 2.
  Option B — Produce a NotifyUserReply(success=false) manually via kafka-ui.

What each step proves:
  2. order created, payment succeeds
  3. peek payment.commands.refund → RefundCommand published with the right paymentId
  4. saga = FAILED (compensated terminal)
  5. order = CANCELLED
  6. orders_saga_terminal_total{outcome="compensated"} incremented

item.name: 3. kafka-ui — peek payment.commands.refund
item.description:
Give the saga ~10s to advance to COMPENSATING before running this.
Expected: at least one RefundCommand with the saga's paymentId.

exec: pm.test('at least one refund message exists', () => msgs.length > 0);
const val = r.data && r.data.result && r.data.result[0] && r.data.result[0].value && r.data.result[0].value[1];

item.name: F4. Flow — Checkout (Mock provider) — payment-gateway Phase 1
item.description:
The provider-aware checkout flow with the mock payment provider.
Mock is synchronous: amount < 50000 → CAPTURED, amount in [50k,100k) → DECLINED,
amount >= 100k → FAILED. Thresholds live in payment-service application.yml
under payment.mock.*.

Flow A (happy): quantity=1 at ₹9.99/unit → amount ₹9.99 → CAPTURED → saga NOTIFIED.
Flow B (decline): quantity=6000 → amount ~₹59,940 → DECLINED → saga FAILED.

What each step proves:
  1. OAuth2 token exchange                     — gateway + auth-server up
  2. POST /api/v1/checkout provider=mock        — new CheckoutController wired
  3. Peek payment row by orderId                — new PaymentQueryController + MockPaymentProvider
  4. Poll saga state                            — Mock reply flowed back through Kafka
  5. Order final status                         — orchestrator advanced correctly
  6. Prometheus — terminal{completed}++         — business metric records the outcome
  7. Flow B: checkout with decline-triggering amount — repeats to confirm failure path
  8. Peek payment row → DECLINED                — Mock rule triggered

item.name: 2. POST /api/v1/checkout — provider=mock, HAPPY
item.description:
Hits the new CheckoutController. order-service:
  - creates Order
  - calls OrderSagaOrchestrator.start(orderId, amount, "mock")
  - orchestrator fires PaymentCommand on payment.commands with provider="mock"
payment-service's PaymentCommandProcessor delegates to PaymentService → MockPaymentProvider.
Mock returns CAPTURED synchronously because amount (₹9.99) < threshold 50000.
Response: 201 Created, redirectUrl=null (mock is synchronous).

exec: pm.test('no redirectUrl for mock', () => body.redirectUrl === null);

item.name: 3. Peek Payment row — expect CAPTURED
item.description:
GET on the new PaymentQueryController. Returns the Payment row persisted
by payment-service. For the mock flow with amount < 50000, status should be
CAPTURED and failureReason should be null.

exec: // Mock is synchronous but Kafka reply still has to round-trip

item.name: 4. Poll saga state (should advance)
item.description:
Payment CAPTURED → PaymentReply(success=true) → orchestrator transitions saga
to PAID, fires NotifyUserCommand → notification replies ok → saga NOTIFIED.

exec: // Give notification side a few seconds to complete
const val = r.data && r.data.result && r.data.result[0] && r.data.result[0].value && r.data.result[0].value[1];

item.name: 7. POST /api/v1/checkout — provider=mock, DECLINE path
item.description:
Same endpoint, bigger quantity: 6000 × ₹9.99 = ₹59,940, which hits the mock's
DECLINED range [50000, 100000). This exercises the failure path through the
same wiring as Flow B of the existing F2 flow, but via the new /checkout API.

item.name: F5. Flow — Checkout (Stripe) — payment-gateway Phase 2
item.description:
End-to-end Stripe hosted-checkout flow.

Prereqs:
  1. .env has real STRIPE_SECRET_KEY (sk_test_...) and STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET (whsec_...).
  2. PAYMENT_STRIPE_ENABLED=true, then re-source .env and restart payment-service.
  3. In a separate terminal: `stripe listen --forward-to localhost:8091/webhooks/stripe`.
     Keep that terminal visible — it logs the webhook events as they arrive.

Flow:
  1. OAuth2 token.
  2. POST /checkout provider=stripe → response carries a redirectUrl.
  3. Peek Payment row — should be INITIATED with providerRef = cs_test_...
  4. [HUMAN STEP] Open the redirectUrl in a browser, pay with 4242 4242 4242 4242.
  5. Poll Payment row → CAPTURED (webhook arrived + processed).
  6. Final saga → NOTIFIED. Order → PAID.
  7. Prometheus — orders_saga_terminal_total{completed}++.

Debugging:
  - If step 3 shows providerRef still null: payment-service couldn't reach Stripe.
    Check /actuator/health and the paymentservice log.
  - If step 5 stays INITIATED forever: webhook never arrived.
    Check `stripe listen` terminal — is it still running? Did the whsec_ change?
  - Stripe-side history: https://dashboard.stripe.com/test/payments

item.name: 2. POST /api/v1/checkout — provider=stripe
item.description:
CheckoutController creates Order+saga, then synchronously calls payment-service
/initiate (via Feign). payment-service's StripePaymentProvider calls
Stripe.Session.create() with sagaId as Idempotency-Key. Response carries the
hosted checkout URL.

exec: pm.test('redirectUrl is a stripe checkout URL', () =>
console.log('open the redirect URL to pay:', body.redirectUrl);

item.name: 3. Peek Payment row — expect INITIATED + providerRef
item.description:
The row exists but is not yet CAPTURED. providerRef is the Stripe Checkout
session id (cs_test_...). redirectUrl is persisted so a client who missed
the HTTP response can still retrieve it from here.

item.name: 4. [HUMAN] Open the redirectUrl and pay with 4242
item.description:
Not a request to send from Postman — open the URL in a BROWSER.
Test card details:
  Card:   4242 4242 4242 4242
  Expiry: anything in the future (e.g. 12/34)
  CVC:    anything (e.g. 123)
  Email:  anything

After payment, Stripe redirects to STRIPE_SUCCESS_URL. The webhook arrives
at payment-service via `stripe listen` within a second or two.

item.name: 5. Poll Payment row until CAPTURED
item.description:
After you've paid in the browser, this should show CAPTURED. If it still
shows INITIATED after 10s, check your `stripe listen` terminal — the webhook
must be arriving there.

exec: // Give Stripe + webhook delivery a moment
// Notification side takes a bit more time
const val = r.data && r.data.result && r.data.result[0] && r.data.result[0].value && r.data.result[0].value[1];
if (replay === 'true') console.log('IDEMPOTENCY REPLAY — handler did not re-run');

item.name: Replay same order (idempotency demo)
item.description: Pins the same Idempotency-Key for both requests. Second call returns the stored response with `Idempotency-Replay: true` and does NOT create a new order.

exec: // Reuse the previously-created key instead of generating a new one.
console.warn('Run "Create order" first to prime the key.');
